description: Single-DGX-Spark Qwen3.8-27B on Ash Hart's TensorFold 1.2.3, the native Zig engine from the creator's linux-aarch64 release archive (exact decoding; its CUDA kernels, sm_121 included, are built into the binary, so nothing compiles at start), with Vontra's MLX 4-bit (group 64) checkpoint and z-lab's DFlash2 draft model, launched as upstream documents it (serve the checkpoint with --drafter naming DFlash2). One rank. Upstream's serve defaults apply: a 32,768-token context (raise the context setting up to the model's 262,144 tokens, subject to TensorFold's startup memory check) and --parallel auto, which shares decode rounds among up to eight streams as memory allows and reports the accepted count at startup. Image input (--vision) is an opt-in option for JPEG, PNG and WebP images; the image carries the exact libjpeg-turbo 3.1.4.1 and libwebp 1.6.0 decoders TensorFold pins. Upstream measured 89.1 tok/s code and 47.2 tok/s chat sampled with DFlash2 on a 48 GB M5 Pro with TensorFold 1.2.1 (upstream claims, other hardware; unmeasured here). Needs NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0). Structured output and required tool calls use the archive's libtfgrammar (xgrammar 0.2.8). The declared memory envelope is carried over from the 0.6.6 recipe and is an estimate until the hardware sweep measures this engine. Licences, for information: Qwen3.8-27B and the Vontra conversion are Apache-2.0; z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 states Apache-2.0 on its model card (a mirror of incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2); TensorFold is Apache-2.0 from 0.6.0 (MIT up to 0.5.0). Thinking is chosen per request (chat template kwargs or sampling parameters), not as a recipe option; server default: Open a think block by default (upstream default: --thinking).
title: Qwen3.8 27B TensorFold single Spark
